recipes.name: Alan Adler Original
recipes.description: Alan Adler's original Aeropress recipe — the one printed on the box. Produces a concentrated shot (not filter coffee) at a narrow 1:4.5 ratio. Add hot water for an Americano, or drink as-is for an intense, clean cup.

phases.label: Pour + Stir
phases.note: Pour all water at once to fill between level 1.5 and 2 on the chamber. Stir gently with the paddle for 10 seconds. Insert plunger immediately — no steep phase.

phases.label: Press
phases.note: Press slowly with the natural weight of your hands, 20-40 seconds. Stop at the hiss. Dilute with hot water for Americano style.

recipes.name: Hoffmann Aeropress
recipes.description: James Hoffmann's ultimate Aeropress recipe. Uses a higher ratio that produces a clean, tea-like cup. Light agitation, no pressing until the very end, and a gentle swirl to break the crust.

phases.label: Pour
phases.note: Add all water at once. Wait 2 minutes. Swirl gently to break the crust. Wait 30 seconds. Insert plunger and press gently — stop at the hiss.

recipes.name: April 4-Pour
recipes.description: Patrik Rolf's signature four-pour method for the April Brewer. Uses a coarse grind and moderate temperature. Each pour is timed: 70g bloom, then 100g, 50g, and 30g with a final spin. The April Brewer's flat bottom and specific hole pattern produce a clean, sweet, and repeatable cup.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Wet all grounds with a wide circular motion. No swirling during bloom.

phases.label: Final Pour + Spin
phases.note: Circular pour. After the 30g pour, lift the brewer slightly and give a gentle spin.

recipes.name: April Base Recipe (Sustainable Profile)
recipes.description: April Coffee's foundational Sustainable Profile — their recommended baseline for the April Brewer. Two equal 100 g pours (each split into a 60 g circle pour followed by a 40 g center pour) produce a clean, balanced cup. Target TDS 1.25–1.35%, total brew time 2:00–3:00. Grind reference: Comandante ~9 clicks (medium-coarse). For a simpler approach, each 100 g phase can be poured in a single continuous circle instead of the circle+center split.

phases.label: First Pour
phases.note: 60 g circle pour then 40 g center pour; start timer at 0:00

phases.label: Second Pour
phases.note: 60 g circle pour then 40 g center pour at 0:30; let draw down

recipes.name: Hoffmann Chemex
recipes.description: James Hoffmann's Chemex recipe. The thick paper and large brewer call for a coarser grind and longer brew time. A single bloom + continuous pour approach suits the Chemex's slower flow rate.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Circular pour, then swirl vigorously to saturate all grounds

phases.label: Main Pour
phases.note: Continuous pour in concentric circles, reaching 500g by ~2:00. Gently stir once after pouring, then let draw down. Remove filter when water stream breaks to drops.

recipes.name: HARIO Filter-in Bottle Cold Brew
recipes.description: HARIO's standard Filter-in Bottle recipe is a gentle eight-hour refrigerated immersion with an integrated strainer and a clean, ready-to-pour finish.

phases.label: Fill
phases.note: Put the coffee in the strainer, assemble the bottle, and gently pour in the cold water

phases.label: Mix and steep
phases.note: Stopper the bottle, shake gently to mix, and refrigerate for 8 hours

phases.label: Serve
phases.note: Shake gently once more, remove the spout, and serve fresh

recipes.name: James Hoffmann Decant Cold Brew
recipes.description: James Hoffmann's low-waste cold brew uses a fine grind, optional fining agent, and careful decanting instead of passing the finished coffee through a filter.

phases.label: Combine
phases.note: Add room-temperature water and stir thoroughly; optionally mix in 10 drops of fining agent

phases.label: Steep and settle
phases.note: Cover and refrigerate for 12 hours so the grounds settle at the bottom

phases.label: Decant
phases.note: Gently pour into a clean carafe and stop before the coffee sediment reaches the rim

recipes.name: Röststätte Classic Cold Brew
recipes.description: Röststätte's classic immersion method produces a sweet, full-bodied cold brew with a simple 1:10 ratio and at least twelve hours of extraction.

phases.label: Combine
phases.note: Add the water to the freshly ground coffee and stir thoroughly until every ground is wet

phases.label: Steep
phases.note: Cover and steep for at least 12 hours in the refrigerator or at room temperature

phases.label: Filter
phases.note: Pass the brew through a fine filter, then store it in the refrigerator

recipes.name: THE BARN Mizudashi Cold Brew
recipes.description: THE BARN's room-temperature Mizudashi method emphasizes sweetness and texture with a 1:10 ratio and a long seventeen-hour extraction.

phases.label: Saturate
phases.note: Add the water in three stages through the Mizudashi filter, stirring so every ground contacts the water

phases.label: Steep
phases.note: Cover and brew at room temperature for a total of 17 hours

phases.label: Finish
phases.note: Remove the grounds, swirl the carafe to distribute the coffee evenly, and serve over ice or chill

recipes.name: The Negotiator
recipes.description: Matteo D'Ottavio's competition-proven Orea recipe that uses the "negotiated" flat filter technique — manually shaping the filter to sit flush inside the brewer for zero-bypass extraction. Five measured pours with precise timing produce a sweet, high-extraction cup with excellent clarity. Works best with light-roast coffees.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Negotiate filter into brewer; 3× coffee weight circular pour bloom with gentle swirl

phases.label: Second Pour
phases.note: Circular pour, let water drop ~1 cm above bed

phases.label: Final Pour
phases.note: Gentle center pour; target total draw-down ~3:30

recipes.name: Big Boy The Base
recipes.description: The base Big Boy recipe for 2+ cups. Three big pours at a 6–7 G/S pour rate keep the wide 8cm bed saturated. Don't pour too slowly — feed the beast. Uses Big Boy Wave filters.

recipes.name: Big Boy The Litre
recipes.description: One whole litre of coffee for 4+ people. Four large pours on the Big Boy with Wave filters. Keep the pour rate up — this is not the time for gentle trickling.

recipes.name: Big Boy The Pulse
recipes.description: A 4-pulse recipe for the Big Boy with Wave filters. One pour per minute keeps the bed refreshed. Don't pour too slowly — maintain good water volume over the wide bed.

recipes.name: V3 Base Two
recipes.description: The classic V3 pulse recipe with Wave filter. Four even spiral pours bring out balance in a bigger cup. Familiar if transitioning from V60 or Kalita.

recipes.name: O1 Easy Does It
recipes.description: The go-to O1 pulse recipe with Flat filter + Negotiator. Five gentle spiral pours — adapt grind and temperature to taste. For Wave filters, grind a little finer.

recipes.name: O1 The Bright
recipes.description: An easy 3-pour recipe for the O1 with Wave filter. The 75/75/150 cadence makes a bright cup with minimal effort — perfect for sleepy mornings.

recipes.name: O1 The Bypass
recipes.description: Matteo D'Ottavio's bypass recipe for the O1 with Wave filter. Circular-to-central pours followed by 15–30g bypass water added to the brewed coffee. Less bypass for intensity, more for smoothness.

phases.label: Bypass
phases.note: Add 15–30g water directly to brewed coffee, to taste

recipes.name: O1 The Techno
recipes.description: Mordy's progressive recipe for the O1 with Flat filter + Negotiator. Pours go from circular to mixed to central, and from bigger to smaller. For Wave filters, grind slightly finer.

recipes.name: V3 Base One
recipes.description: A simple 4-pulse recipe for the V3 with Wave filter. Big brightness, lower sweetness, light body — familiar if transitioning from V60 or Kalita.

recipes.name: V3 The Bright
recipes.description: A super-easy 3-pour recipe on the V3 with Wave filter. The 75/75/150 pouring cadence makes a bright, happy cup with minimal effort — perfect for sleepy mornings.

recipes.name: V3 The Fine
recipes.description: A community-favourite single-pour recipe on the V3 with Wave filter. First 50g in a slow circular pour, then 150g as a slow central pour. Very quick — always under 2 minutes.

phases.label: Pour
phases.note: First 50g slow circular, remaining 150g slow central pour

recipes.name: V3 The Ice
recipes.description: A flash-brew iced recipe on the V3 with Wave filter. Brew 160ml over 140g of ice in the carafe. Four gentle spiral pours produce a bright, fruity flash brew that doesn't taste diluted. Stir and cool rapidly after brewing.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Gentle spiral pour onto 140g ice in carafe

recipes.name: V3 The Mid
recipes.description: A simple 3-pour recipe for the V3 with Flat filter + Negotiator. Half circular, half central pours work great for washed coffees and can handle naturals too. Control extraction time with pouring flow rate.

recipes.name: V3 The Pulse
recipes.description: A simple pulse recipe on the V3 with Flat filter + Negotiator. Five gentle spiral pours — adjust grind and temperature to taste.

recipes.name: V3 The Wide
recipes.description: A high-extraction, wide-ratio recipe for the V3 with Flat filter + Negotiator. Half circular, half central pours. Works best with washed coffees — adapt grind and pouring speed if drawdown is slow.

recipes.name: V4 Dara For Two
recipes.description: The Dara scaled for two cups on the V4 Open Bottom. Same balanced profile, larger batch.

recipes.name: V4 The Dara
recipes.description: A recipe by DARA from Madrid for the V4 Open Bottom. Balanced and consistent results across all coffee types. Scale up to 18g by pouring to 60g/135g/225g/300g.

recipes.name: V4 Easy Does It
recipes.description: The go-to V4 pulse recipe. Five even pours at ~50g each keep the structure simple and repeatable. Works with Fast Bottom and Flat filter + Negotiator; grind coarser for Classic Bottom, add central pouring for Open/Apex.

recipes.name: V4 Easy For Two
recipes.description: Easy Does It scaled up for two cups. Grind coarser than the single-cup version and maintain a steady 5 G/S pour rate throughout.

recipes.name: V4 Fine For Two
recipes.description: The Fine scaled up for two cups using Sibarist Fast Flat filters. Bloom then one very slow continuous pour at 3 G/S — maintain a small water column, replacing water as it drains.

phases.label: Long Pour
phases.note: Spiral pour very slowly at 3 G/S — maintain water level, replace as it drains

recipes.name: V4 The Four Six
recipes.description: Tetsu Kasuya's 4:6 method adapted for the V4 Wide + Fast Bottom. A framework, not just a recipe — swap the first two pour sizes for more sweetness, or split the last pour into three for more strength. Uses Flat filter + Negotiator.

recipes.name: V4 OG Base #2
recipes.description: A flexible recipe from the V2 era, carried forward on the V4 Classic Bottom + Wave filter. Loved most with washed coffees. Grind finer for Fast Bottom, add central pours for Open/Apex.

recipes.name: V4 OG Iced
recipes.description: An iced pour-over on the V4 Classic Bottom + Wave filter. Brew 160ml over 140g of ice in the carafe for a bright, fruity flash brew. Swirl and stir after brewing, let the ice dilute to taste.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Circular pour onto 140g ice in carafe

recipes.name: V4 So Soft
recipes.description: A conical recipe for the V4 Wide + Apex Bottom using Sibarist Fast Conical filter. Soft and clean results that work for many coffee types. The first pour starts circular then shifts central.

recipes.name: V4 The Aussie
recipes.description: Inspired by Australian Brewers Cup competitors — dose up, grind coarse, pour fast. Works well for fermented coffees where you want to tame boozy notes and reach a tea-like body. Pour next when you see the dry coffee bed appear.

recipes.name: V4 The Bypass
recipes.description: A bypass recipe by UK Brewing Champion Matteo D'Ottavio for the V4 Open Bottom. After three circular-to-central pours, 15–30g of bypass water is added directly to the brewed coffee to taste. Bypass less for intensity, more for smoothness.

phases.label: Bypass
phases.note: Add 15–30g water directly to brewed coffee, to taste

recipes.name: V4 The Champ
recipes.description: Martin Wölfl's World Brewers Cup 2024 winning recipe on the V4 Narrow + Fast Bottom. Uses a Melodrip Drip Assist at 6 G/S pouring speed with Sibarist Fast Flat filter.

recipes.name: V4 The Fine
recipes.description: A two-pour recipe for sweet, punchy, juicy washed coffees. Bloom then one long slow pour at 4 G/S. Best with Wave filter; grind coarser for Flat + Negotiator. Not recommended for naturals or fermented coffees at this fine grind.

phases.label: Long Pour
phases.note: Pour slowly at 4 G/S in a spiral to 260g

recipes.name: V4 The Hangover
recipes.description: When you need 500+ ml of coffee. Five slow circular pours on the V4 Fast Bottom + Wave filter. Slow your pour rate slightly — there's a lot of coffee in the brewer. Works for one, two, or three thirsty people.

recipes.name: V4 The Techno
recipes.description: A progressive recipe by Mordy for the V4 Open Bottom — pours go from bigger to smaller, and from circular to mixed to central. Best with Flat filter + Negotiator or Open/Apex Bottom.

recipes.name: V4 Two Aussies
recipes.description: The Aussie scaled up for two. Slow down pouring speed to standard 5 G/S since there's more coffee and liquid. Adjust ratio by taste — increase dose or grind finer if too thin.

recipes.name: Z1 Easy Does It
recipes.description: The go-to Z1 pulse recipe using the Melodrip dish (mandatory). Five even pours keep it simple and repeatable. For dense washed coffee, combine last 2 pours into one 100g pour; for soluble naturals, go 2 clix coarser and use 18g dose.

recipes.name: Z1 The Four Six
recipes.description: Tetsu Kasuya's 4:6 method adapted for the Z1 via Melodrip. Five pours with an easy framework — swap first two pour sizes for more brightness, or pour evenly for balance.

recipes.name: Z1 Lazy Sunday
recipes.description: An easy 3-pour recipe for the Z1 via Melodrip. Kick back on lazy weekends. Make it Extra Lazy: skip the bloom, pour in two 125g pours with a slightly finer grind and slower speed.

recipes.name: Z1 The Aussie
recipes.description: The Aussie method on the Z1 via Melodrip — dose up, grind coarse, pour fast. Pour next when you see the dry coffee bed appear. Great for taming boozy notes in fermented coffees.

recipes.name: Z1 The Champ
recipes.description: Martin Wölfl's World Brewers Cup 2024 winning recipe adapted for the Z1 via Melodrip. Enlarge pours and increase flow rate as the brew progresses. Juicy, high-quality results.

phases.label: Final Pour
phases.note: Circular pour via Melodrip, increase flow rate

recipes.name: Z1 The Clever
recipes.description: An immersion recipe for the Z1 with Switch adapter, adapted from James Hoffmann's Clever method. Add water first, then coffee on top — stir gently to saturate. No Melodrip needed. Steep 2 minutes then open valve.

phases.label: Add Coffee
phases.note: Close valve, add 166ml water, then 10g coffee on top. Stir gently to saturate

recipes.name: Z1 The Dara
recipes.description: DARA's balanced recipe adapted for the Z1 via Melodrip. Scale up to 18g by pouring to 60g/135g/225g/300g. Try grinding slightly coarser and pouring slower for a different cup profile.

recipes.name: Z1 The Fine
recipes.description: A two-pour high-extraction recipe for the Z1 via Melodrip. Bloom then one long slow pour at 3 G/S. Great for washed coffees — go finer for more intensity, or explore lower temps (86–88°C) as you grind finer.

phases.label: Long Pour
phases.note: Spiral pour slowly at 3 G/S via Melodrip

recipes.name: Z1 The Hybrid
recipes.description: A hybrid percolation-immersion recipe by Matteo D'Ottavio for the Z1 with Switch adapter. Percolate the first two pours, then close the valve for a final immersion. Steep longer for more body, shorter for lighter texture.

phases.label: Bloom — Valve Closed
phases.note: Close valve, spiral pour via Melodrip

phases.label: Second Pour — Valve Open
phases.note: Open valve, spiral pour via Melodrip

recipes.name: Z1 The Micro
recipes.description: A full-immersion recipe for the Z1 with Switch adapter. Open valve for a short bloom, then close and fill the chamber. Simple and clean results for any coffee type.

phases.label: Bloom — Valve Open
phases.note: Open valve, spiral pour 20g via Melodrip

phases.label: Immersion Pour — Valve Closed
phases.note: Close valve, spiral pour 150g slowly at 3 G/S

recipes.name: Z1 The Pulse
recipes.description: A classic 5-pulse recipe on the Z1 via Melodrip. Easy to remember — 40/80/120/160/200g. Scale up to 15g (50/100/150/200/250) or 18g (60/120/180/240/300).

recipes.name: Z1 The Scandi
recipes.description: A super-simple 2-pour recipe on the Z1 via Melodrip. Two big fast circular pours — 100g in 20 seconds each. Easy, quick, and surprisingly balanced. Add 2g coffee and grind coarser for more intensity with cleanliness.

phases.label: First Pour
phases.note: Circular pour within 20 seconds via Melodrip

phases.label: Second Pour
phases.note: Circular pour within 20 seconds via Melodrip

recipes.name: Z1 The Tetsu
recipes.description: Tetsu Kasuya's Switch recipe adapted for the Z1 with Switch adapter. Uses two water temperatures — 94°C for the first three pours, then 80°C for the final immersion pour. If you have one kettle, add cold water after the third pour.

phases.label: Second Pour — Valve Open
phases.note: Open valve, circular pour to 120g at 94°C

phases.label: Immersion Pour — Valve Closed
phases.note: Close valve, circular pour to 300g at 80°C

recipes.name: IARO Beginner Origami Wave Method
recipes.description: IARO's beginner method uses a Kalita Wave filter in an Origami dripper. The medium grind and slow circular pour are designed for a simple, even brew. The archive standardizes the serving at 15g coffee and 250g water because the source article does not specify a dose or total water amount.

phases.label: Circular Pour
phases.note: Pour slowly in a circular motion to wet and extract the coffee evenly

recipes.name: ORIGAMI Dripper with THE COFFEESHOP Vol.2
recipes.description: Daichi Hagiwara's six-pour recipe for the classic ORIGAMI S dripper. Uses a distinctive 10-second pour / 10-second wait rhythm after a stirred bloom. Honduras Los Pinos Typica Honey coffee offers a silky mouthfeel, jasmine-like florals, and fruit notes of lemon and green apple. The spoon stir during bloom ensures all grounds are saturated evenly.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Circular pour, stir 5 times with spoon

recipes.name: ORIGAMI Dripper with FUGLEN Vol.1
recipes.description: Mika Jackson's hybrid pour recipe for the ORIGAMI Air S dripper. Starts with circular pours then switches to a single-point center pour — a technique that builds body while preserving clarity. Kenya AA KANGOCHO delivers black currant and stone fruit notes with a jammy sweetness, roasted in FUGLEN's signature Nordic style from Oslo.

phases.label: Center Pour
phases.note: Center pour to 250g, then stir to homogenize

recipes.name: ORIGAMI Dripper with KOPIKALYAN Vol.3
recipes.description: Masashi Nishio's five-pour recipe for the ORIGAMI Air S dripper. Features WANOJA KAMOJANG West Java anaerobic honey-process coffee — expect rich grape-like flavor, juicy fruitiness, and a long-lasting sweetness with depth. The circular pour technique works with the dripper's ribbed design for even extraction.

recipes.name: ORIGAMI Dripper with Wave Filter
recipes.description: ORIGAMI's wave-filter recipe uses a medium-coarse grind and three pours at 30-second intervals. The wave filter keeps the paper close to the dripper, supporting a stable flow and a balanced, full-bodied cup.

phases.label: First Pour
phases.note: Pour wide and evenly across the bed

phases.label: Second Pour
phases.note: Pour wide and evenly across the bed

phases.label: Third Pour
phases.note: Pour gently in the center, then let draw down

recipes.name: Hoffmann 1-Cup V60
recipes.description: James Hoffmann's refined single-cup V60 technique. Uses boiling water and a pulsed pouring approach with gentle swirls between pours. The well in the coffee bed and the final swirl ensure even extraction.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Spiral pour. Swirl gently at 0:10-0:15 to knock grounds off walls

phases.label: Final Pour
phases.note: Spiral pour. Swirl gently to flatten bed, let draw down

recipes.name: Matt Perger V60
recipes.description: Matt Perger's high-extraction V60 method from his 2013 championship work. Notable for aggressively stirring the bloom and grinding finer than typical pour-over recipes. Targets ~20.8% extraction.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Pour then stir vigorously in a cross-pattern to maximize saturation

phases.label: Final Pour
phases.note: Spiral pour. When water drains halfway, tap/swirl to flatten bed ("Rao spin")

recipes.name: Osmotic Flow V60
recipes.description: The Japanese osmotic flow method emphasizes keeping the water level just above the coffee bed throughout the brew, creating a gentle osmotic extraction. A single, very slow continuous pour with precise kettle control.

phases.label: Bloom
phases.note: Create a small crater in the center, center pour gently into it

phases.label: Osmotic Pour
phases.note: Single slow continuous center pour, keeping water just 1-2cm above the bed. Takes about 2 minutes. Do not disturb the crust.

recipes.name: Tetsu Kasuya 4:6 Method
recipes.description: Tetsu Kasuya's winning 2016 World Brewers Cup recipe. The first 40% of water controls flavor balance (sweetness vs acidity), the remaining 60% controls strength/body. Let each pour fully drain before starting the next.

phases.label: Bloom (40% — sweetness)
phases.note: Circular pour ~10s. Smaller bloom emphasizes sweetness; larger bloom emphasizes acidity

recipes.name: The Barn 1-Cup V60
recipes.description: The Barn Berlin's daily-driver V60 recipe. A simple, repeatable pulsed-pour approach. Keep pours within the "bagel ring" of the coffee bed and avoid hitting the paper filter edges.

phases.label: Pulse Pours
phases.note: Circular pour. Three ~50g pours, pulsing gently between each
